crime_highlights: the accused produced a knife and stabbed Mr. Corbett in the left groin area
It immediately disabled him, and he collapsed.
He felt the blood on his pants.
rationale_highlights: such hardships and deprivations, while not unique to individual indigenous persons, were visited wholesale upon them as a people
They were largely the result of laws and policies which were formed and animated by racism.

this court and society at large must try to understand how Mr. Ryan’s upbringing, how his experience as an indigenous person in a society which marginalized and humiliated Mi’kmaq people may have contributed to Rein’s actions on the night in question
note: Court discusses Gladue at length but never says it reduced culpability or sentence

crime_highlights: Mr. Beals, who was proceeding northbound in his vehicle, entered the centre lane and collided head on with the car being driven by Ms. Isles
Ms. Isles had her two infant children in her vehicle.
Ms. Isles suffered a concussion and was very sore as a result of the impact.
In addition, her tongue was split in half. She required 20 stitches to put her tongue back together.
rationale_highlights: there are a number of significant mitigating factors in relation to the offender, Mr. Beals, which were highlighted in the very positive Pre-Sentence Report and in the Impact of Race and Cultural Assessment Report
this sentencing decision ought to be balanced through the imposition of a sentence that also assists in the rehabilitation of Mr. Beals
note: IRCA summarised; race factors absent from mitigating list; no stated effect

crime_highlights: Mr. Rhodenizer was in possession of the above-noted firearms, but he also had possession of non-restricted firearms – one being a loaded semi-automatic Remington .22 calibre rifle
His possession of all of those firearms in the circumstances of this case was, in my opinion, designed to amass an arsenal which would, if necessary, be produced to intimidate or confront others.
rationale_highlights: I find that the Mitigating Circumstances are as follows

Mr. Rhodenizer is an aboriginal offender who has personally experienced and been affected by many Gladue factors, which have plagued aboriginal communities, including family breakdown; domestic violence; physical mental and emotional abuse; poverty

the Crown Attorney revised his sentencing position to recommend a total sentence of 30 months taking into account several Gladue factors which, in all likelihood, contributed to Mr. Kyle Rhodenizer’s involvement in this criminal activity

the Crown Attorney’s revised sentencing recommendations which took into account several Gladue factors present in this case and reflect the particular attention to the circumstances of aboriginal offenders
I find that the total sentence of 30 months is a “just and appropriate” sanction
note: Court lists Gladue factors as mitigating; adopts sentence reduced from 36 to 30 months
